comment: Shared det-state chunk-geometry vectors: the genesis-authoring rules every conforming validator must reproduce. The ceremony geometry mirrors the frozen ceremony model (d_model 1536, 24 layers, vocab 32768, qdim 1536, swiglu hidden 4608; registration order: token embedding; per block attn-norm, wq, wk, wv, wo, ffn-norm, w1, w3, w2; final norm). The norm parameters ARE d_model wide, so the profile chunk must divide 1536 itself; a chunk that divides the matrices but not d_model (e.g. 4096) is refused at the first norm parameter.

profile_chunk_vectors.name: acceptance-tier chunk 64 divides every ceremony numel
chunk 1536 (= d_model) is the widest norm-compatible chunk
profile default 4096 divides the matrices but NOT the 1536-wide norms
chunk 3072 exceeds d_model and cannot divide the norms

state_chunk_size_vectors.name: chunk 64: 4 MiB is exactly 16384 compression-chunk widths
chunk 1536: 682 x 6144 B is the ~4 MiB multiple
chunk 1536: a bare 4 MiB is not a 6144 B multiple
chunk 64: off-by-one is not a 256 B multiple
one chunk width is the smallest legal size
zero state chunk size is degenerate

cadence_retention_vectors.name: cadence 4 + one churn slot fits retention 8
cadence 4 + one churn slot exceeds retention 7
cadence 3 strands a rejoiner past retention 5
cadence 5 exceeds the retained record horizon 4 (c15f: churn recovery impossible by construction)
cadence 8 exceeds the retained record horizon even with unbounded retention
retention 0 = unbounded, no payload constraint (cadence within the horizon)
cadence 0 = remote publication disabled, nothing to bound
